text:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a big latency spike on snapshot restores for tenant-342. Several restores from snapshot-2026-03-20 are hanging during decrypt and failing with KMS timeouts (504). Started ~09:10 UTC after yesterday's RBAC cleanup.

kevin: ugh. which KMS key? any error snippets?

maria: key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345. Log excerpt:```
2026-03-21T09:11:02Z ERROR restore: decrypt failed: kms response error: StatusCode=504, RequestID=xyz-123, message=GatewayTimeout
2026-03-21T09:11:02Z WARN restore: fallback attempted to software-decrypt but payload sealed with KMS-only key
```

sanjay: Yesterday PR #4822 removed a set of legacy service-account grants from that key. Did the RBAC cleanup include the backup-uploader role?

maria: I think so — I linked the PR in the incident ticket: https://git.company/infra/pr/4822. The change removed an IAM policy binding for `backup-uploader@infra` that had kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey permissions.

olivia: That would explain it. When the uploader loses `kms:GenerateDataKey`, envelope-decrypt flow stalls because the restore path requests a data key via KMS on-demand. If the grant was removed, KMS either returns AccessDenied or times out if there are cross-account grant lookups.

kevin: Are we seeing AccessDenied anywhere in CloudTrail?

maria: Checked CloudTrail for the key, but we have gaps during 09:05–09:12 — nothing logged for the backup-uploader principal. Looks like audit ingestion delayed due to downstream analytics job restart (tracking in infra-alerts). So we don't have clean evidence yet.

encops-bot: :warning: ALERT: snapshot-restore-latency breached SLO (p95 > 4s) for tenant-342 — incident #INC-2026-167 created.

sanjay: Two things to do now: 1) temp fix: re-grant kms:Decrypt + kms:GenerateDataKey to `backup-uploader@infra` as an inline policy on the key so restores can proceed; 2) longer-term: update RBAC cleanup to whitelist active service principals and add a post-cleanup smoke test hitting a decrypt path.

olivia: For the temp grant, use the KMS grant approach so we can revoke quickly:```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id abcd-ef01-2345 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey --name temp-restore-grant
```
That avoids IAM policy churn. After restore success, delete the grant.

kevin: will open the grant now. Also: maria, can you run a canary restore into staging with the temp grant to confirm?

maria: running now. If this passes I'll push a rollback of the RBAC change for that principal and create a narrow follow-up PR to re-introduce granting via managed role mapping.

kevin: one more ask — audit. We need to ensure CloudTrail covers KMS events and CloudWatch agent for the backup service is healthy. sanjay, can you own the audit gaps and ticket infra-alerts?

sanjay: on it. I'll check CloudTrail delivery status and the analytics ingestion job. Command I'll run: `aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name company-main` and `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345`

olivia: After the temp grant and a successful canary, we should also add a smoke test to CI that performs `aws kms generate-data-key` -> envelope encrypt -> restore to catch RBAC regressions during PRs that touch infra IAM.

maria: Canary succeeded, restores are back to normal. I'll post the rollback PR in 10m and add notes to the incident.

kevin: thanks. we'll follow up with a short postmortem: root cause = RBAC cleanup removed active grant; contributing = audit ingestion gap. Action items: temp KMS grant, RBAC whitelist + smoke test, CloudTrail ingestion alert.

encops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident #INC-2026-167 updated: mitigation applied (temp grant), monitoring restored.

maria: filing postmortem doc now and tagging sec+infra. :memo:
